flashcard_questions.q: What was the magnitude of the 2010 Haiti earthquake?
Which two plates meet at the boundary beneath Haiti?
flashcard_questions.a: The Caribbean Plate and the North American Plate.

flashcard_questions.q: How many people were killed by the 2010 Haiti earthquake?
How many people were left homeless by the 2010 Haiti earthquake?
How many buildings were destroyed in the 2010 Haiti earthquake?
What share of Haiti's population was left without work after the earthquake?
What was Haiti's GNI per capita at the time of the 2010 earthquake?
Which country took over the relief effort after the 2010 Haiti earthquake?
What share of the $1.1 billion raised by aid agencies reached Haiti?
What was the magnitude of the 2011 Christchurch earthquake?
How many people were killed by the 2011 Christchurch earthquake?
How much did insurance companies pay out after the Christchurch earthquake?
Which body was created to coordinate rebuilding after the Christchurch earthquake?
Why did Haiti suffer far more deaths than Christchurch from a similar earthquake?
flashcard_questions.a: Haiti's buildings were poorly built with almost no earthquake-resistant design, so they collapsed.

flashcard_questions.q: Which of the Three Ps means designing buildings to withstand an earthquake?

notes: 15 cards: 12 case-study-to-fact carrying one figure or named body each, with the earthquake named in every question (7 Haiti, 4 Christchurch, 1 plate boundary), 1 cause-to-consequence comparing the two death tolls, 1 term card on the Three Ps, 1 relief-response card. Every figure is taken exactly as the lesson states it. New Zealand's GNI, the Christchurch building-damage count, the primary/secondary effect definitions and the one-year recovery statistics were trimmed to stay within 15 and to keep the two magnitude and death-toll pairs from interfering.
